McLaren.summary: McLaren has reshaped the front‑suspension fairings and trimmed the front‑wing flap to tighten up airflow over the car, giving a sharper turn‑in and more consistent grip through the corners. At the rear they’ve fitted a low‑downforce wing package with a slimmer flap and a reduced‑chord beam wing, cutting drag so the car can carry higher straight‑line speed. Together, these aero tweaks should make the car feel more balanced on the circuit’s fast sections while still staying planted in the twisty bits, giving McLaren a better shot at the weekend’s podium.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has trimmed the front‑wing flaps and lightened both the rear and lower “beam” wings, giving the car a cleaner aerodynamic shape that reduces drag. The changes should boost straight‑line speed while keeping enough downforce to stay stable through the corners, meaning the team will be able to push harder on the lap and fight more aggressively for position this weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has tweaked the front wing by shortening its outer flaps, giving the car a tighter, more responsive front end that helps it bite into corners earlier. The whole floor has been reshaped – the surface, the little “fences” that manage the airflow, and the edge wing profile have all been refined – to smooth the air under the car, boost down‑force and keep the rear stable without adding drag. Together, these changes should translate into better cornering grip and more consistent lap times for this weekend’s race.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has tweaked three aero pieces for this weekend: the rear‑wing tip now has a finer shape to shave off a bit of drag, the outboard floor fence has been re‑angled to smooth the airflow under the car, and the front‑wing flap has been slightly flattened to reduce front‑end load. These subtle changes should give the car a cleaner‑looking rear and more balanced handling, helping it stay glued to the tarmac through the high‑speed corners and improve overall lap times.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has added a fresh rear‑wing flap that’s less aggressive, giving them a finer “drag range” to match this weekend’s circuit. In plain terms, the car can now generate a bit more downforce for the slower corners without costing too much straight‑line speed on the long straights. The result should be a tighter, more stable car that can push harder through the high‑speed sections while still staying glued to the track where it matters most.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has installed a new, circuit‑specific front wing that lets the team fine‑tune the car’s balance for this track. The extra adjustability should improve corner‑entry grip and overall stability, giving the drivers a better chance to fight for higher positions in qualifying and the race.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls have tweaked the rear wing, under‑floor and side‑pod shapes, plus the mirror housings to suit this circuit’s layout, trimming drag while keeping enough downforce for cornering grip. These aerodynamic refinements should give the car a smoother airflow and a tighter handling feel, helping the team extract more speed on the straights and better stability through the bends this weekend.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams is trialling a small “trim” on the trailing edges of both the front and rear wing flaps, essentially shaving off a bit of drag. That extra low‑drag bite should give the car a higher straight‑line speed on this weekend’s fast sections, while still letting the team fine‑tune the balance if they need a little more grip. In short, it’s a simple tweak aimed at making the car quicker on the straights without sacrificing too much handling.
